title: Beyond Reference Data Conformance—Eligibility, a Reporting Equation and a Verification Procedure for Almen Saturation Curves
content: SAE J2597 tests whether saturation-curve software reproduces reference intensities. That shows computational conformance. It does not show that an individual Almen result is fit to report. This paper proposes four conditions for result eligibility: method qualification, measurement integrity, exposure support and adequacy. We test them on the ten J2597 datasets, on a 388-strip replicated experiment and in simulation. All three J2597 example equations meet the targets, yet they differ in intensity by up to 0.0012 in. Purely multiplicative strip-lot effects scale intensity but leave characteristic exposure unchanged, so checks apply within one lot; additive offsets and lot-dependent shape changes do move it. A gamma mixture of exponential rates, GAM3, contains two J2597 equations as limits and reaches all ten targets within 0.00006 in. In simulations whose truths are rate mixtures or interpolations of the replicated data, fixing its shape parameter from a qualification curve cuts the error in characteristic exposure from about 10% to 4%; these test recovery within its family, not superiority over truths outside it. The saturation curve can be read as a work-hardening law of the impacted layer, an analogy of form. A frozen qualification curve, with verification strips at the exposures where each fault shows, detects drifts that single-strip verification misses. Seventeen provisions are proposed. All thresholds are candidates that need locked implementation and independent validation before use in a standard.
